transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Karen Li (CISO, Riverstone Health); Tom Evans (VP Eng); Priya Shah (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto):
- Security-focused POC scoping to validate Redwood in a regulated healthcare environment; discussion covered SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and retention, network/VPC requirements, benchmarks and success criteria, and timelines for a 4-6 week pilot.

Topics: Success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, VPC networking

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro - I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Morning all, hi, Diego here. We'll mostly focus on the security and infra bits you flagged in the form.
[00:20] Karen Li: Thanks, Maya. I wanted to make sure we cover SOC2 evidence, iso 27001, SSO requirements and audit logs, like what we need to sign off the pilot from a compliance POV.
[00:31] Tom Evans: And just to add, we want to run a quick benchmark against our sample workload to validate latency and cost assumptions before we commit to a dedicated pool.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. High-level plan: short pilot, default 4 weeks, up to 6 if we need extra time. We can run hosted with strict data handling and network restrictions or use Redwood Dedicated or Private - whichever fits your security and cost.
[01:00] Priya Shah: For Riverstone our baseline is: SOC 2 Type II or equivalent attestation, ISO 27001 is a big plus, SSO via SAML 2.0 with our IdP (Okta), RBAC that maps to our internal roles, and immutable audit logs retained for 12-13 months. Also need separation of duties and exportable logs for our SIEM.
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: Understood. We have SOC2 and ISO artifacts - we'll share the attestation pack. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC, and we can map groups to RBAC policies; Diego: I'll send our RBAC template.
[01:35] Karen Li: Can you put in writing the encryption at rest and in transit details, and whether keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM)? We need to show that to legal.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys in Private deployments and in Dedicated via KMS integrations - we'll include the KMS section in the packet. For hosted we do envelope encryption and can discuss dedicated KMS on request.
[01:56] Tom Evans: About benchmarks: we want a realistic workload. Our app typically does 35-45 qps during peak for inference, with average prompt lengths ~220 tokens and some long tails. We expect p95 latency <350 ms for most calls, and cost per 1k tokens should be within the estimates you provided earlier.
[02:18] Priya Shah: Also need to confirm PII handling - we will sanitize but need guarantees on data retention and deletion after the pilot. What are Redwood's retention defaults and deletion paths?
[02:30] Diego Alvarez: Default retention is 30 days for hosted logs and inputs - but for pilots we can configure extended retention and guaranteed deletions; for private/dedicated we can set retention to mirror your policy and provide deletion certificates. I'll note that we'll produce an audit trail for deletions.
[02:45] Karen Li: Good. Also need to know the exact audit events captured - who called the model, which model version, route, tokens in/out (we don't need raw content), IPs, and administrative actions.
[03:00] Diego Alvarez: We log request metadata (route, model id, time, request size, response size, p95 latency), auth identity, and admin actions. Raw request payloads are configurable and can be redacted. We'll provide schema for the audit logs.
[03:18] Maya Chen: For the POC success criteria - let's get explicit: 1) Functional: end-to-end integration with your SSO and RBAC; 2) Performance: p95 latency <350ms on the sample workload for at least 95% of calls, throughput 40 qps sustained; 3) Security: SOC2 artifacts provided and SSO/RBAC validated; 4) Observability: audit logs available and exported to Riverstone SIEM; 5) Cost: hosted pilot cost not to exceed X (we'll put numbers in the estimate).
[03:45] Tom Evans: That sounds reasonable, though we may want 99th latency metrics for long-tail. Also clarify your fallback behavior - if you hit capacity on hosted will you fallback to a smaller model variant or queue requests?
[04:00] Diego Alvarez: We can do smart routing and fallbacks; for a pilot we'll.define policies: can fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant or route to Dedicated in a failover config. We'll include recommended configurations for QoS.
[04:15] Priya Shah: On SSO - our IdP is Okta. We need a SAML metadata file, and we need sample mapping of Okta groups to RBAC roles. Also SCIM for provisioning would be ideal but not required for the pilot.
[04:30] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML and SCIM. For the pilot we'll do SAML for auth and optional SCIM later. I'll send the SAML SP metadata and example attribute mappings.
[04:40] Karen Li: Audit retention 12-13 months is required; are there additional costs for longer retention? Also where are logs stored regionally? We need EU residency for some datasets.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Retention beyond default may incur small storage fees; we'll surface that in the cost estimate. Logs can be stored in-region for Dedicated/Private; hosted can be pinned to region but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll mark this as a requirement.
[05:10] Tom Evans: Let's talk benchmarks - Diego, what do you need from us to run an in-proc benchmark?
[05:17] Diego Alvarez: We'll need a sanitized sample dataset (Prompts + expected behavior), the request/response size distribution, concurrency pattern (rps/qps over time), and a target SLA matrix. Ideally a short spec doc and a small load script or a locust/postman collection.
[05:32] Priya Shah: We'll provide a sample of 10k prompts with distribution and a script to replay spike patterns. But we need to ensure no PHI in the sample - will redact.
[05:42] Diego Alvarez: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll run against a hosted pilot node first and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and memory usage. We'll also run a small Dedicated config if you want to compare.
[05:58] Karen Li: Timeline question: we need compliance review to finish before we start ingesting any data. How fast can you provide SOC2 docs and the SSO setup guide?
[06:10] Maya Chen: We'll send SOC2/ISO pack within 3 business days (target 2026-04-02). Diego will send SAML guide and RBAC template in 5 business days. Once you sign an MSA we can schedule the benchmark for the following week.
[06:25] Tom Evans: On legal and procurement - procurement wants to see data processing addendum and liability clauses. We have a standard checklist; Maya, can you share Redwood's DPA?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include DPA and the standard MSA redlines we've accepted before. I'll attach those to the security packet.
[06:42] Priya Shah: One more network note: Riverstone will require a VPC peering option or private link for traffic; can Redwood support AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for hosted?
[06:52] Diego Alvarez: For hosted we can do TLS over public endpoints and strict IP allowlisting; PrivateLink/VPC peering is available for Dedicated/Private deployments. We'll document the options and recommended approach for the pilot.
[07:05] Karen Li: Ok, sounds like next steps are clear. Recap please?
[07:10] Maya Chen: Quick recap: 1) We (Redwood) send SOC2/ISO packet, DPA, and MSA; 2) Diego sends SAML SSO guide, RBAC mapping, and audit log schema; 3) Riverstone sends sanitized sample dataset, traffic profile, and stakeholders; 4) schedule benchmark for week of 2026-04-12; 5) Redwood provides hosted vs dedicated cost estimates for pilot.
[07:35] Tom Evans: I'd like the benchmark to include a canary with a lower-cost quantized model to compare quality vs cost.
[07:45] Diego Alvarez: Noted - we'll include quantized model variants in the benchmark matrix and capture quality regression metrics tied to your eval set.
[07:56] Priya Shah: And please make sure any logs we receive have deterministic identifiers so we can map events back to our users without exposing raw PII.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We'll redact PII and include hashed identifiers as needed.
[08:18] Karen Li: Who's the point of contact for security docs?
[08:22] Maya Chen: Me, Maya. For technical runbooks and SSO, Diego will be the contact.
[08:28] Tom Evans: Alright, thanks everyone.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the packet and next steps.
[08:35] Diego Alvarez: Thanks, bye.
[08:38] Karen Li: Bye.

References and links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-iso-packet (will be attached), SAML guide: https://redwood.ai/docs/sso-saml, RBAC template: https://redwood.ai/docs/rbac-template, benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/pilot-template

Auto-notes: There were a few transcription glitches - e.g., "K V cache" typed as "K V cash" in one segment; proper nouns (Riverstone) were generally captured but please ignore occasional mis-hearings.

End of transcript.
